subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Control in Everyday Life
description: Learn Control in Everyday Life in one minute.

hook.text: Your body is a control system — temperature, blood pressure, and balance are all regulated by feedback.

buildup.text: Anti-lock brakes pulse 15 times per second, controlling wheel slip to maximize stopping force.

discovery.text: Building HVAC systems use predictive control — adjusting for weather forecasts and occupancy schedules.

twist.text: Drone swarms use distributed control — no central brain, yet they fly in perfect formation.

climax.text: From insulin pumps to power grids, control theory quietly runs the infrastructure of modern life.

punchline.text: Measure, decide, act — control systems keep the world running.

quiz.question: How do anti-lock braking systems (ABS) use feedback control?
options: They lock the wheels completely to maximize friction
They pulse brake pressure rapidly to control wheel slip and maximize stopping force
They apply brakes only to the front wheels
